questions.text: Which organization accredits hospitals through the Joint Commission accreditation program?

options.a: Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS)
options.c: The National Committee for Quality Assurance (NCQA)

questions.explanation: The Joint Commission (TJC) is the primary accreditation body for hospitals and healthcare organizations in the United States.

questions.text: What is the purpose of The Joint Commission's National Patient Safety Goals (NPSGs)?

options.a: To rank hospitals by clinical performance
options.b: To address specific areas of concern in patient safety through evidence-based requirements
options.c: To replace CMS Conditions of Participation

questions.explanation: NPSGs are developed annually to focus healthcare organizations on specific safety practices with the strongest evidence for preventing harm.

questions.text: CMS Conditions of Participation (CoPs) are BEST described as:

options.a: Optional guidelines for improving hospital quality
options.b: Standards that healthcare organizations must meet to participate in Medicare and Medicaid programs
options.c: Billing requirements for submitting claims to CMS

questions.explanation: CoPs are federal regulations that healthcare organizations must comply with to be eligible for Medicare and Medicaid reimbursement.

questions.text: Which of the following is a characteristic of a 'Deemed Status' hospital?

options.a: A hospital that has failed its most recent CMS survey
options.b: A hospital accredited by an approved accreditation body, meeting CMS CoP requirements
options.c: A hospital that operates without any accreditation
options.d: A hospital that exclusively serves Medicare patients

questions.explanation: Deemed status means a hospital accredited by an approved body (e.g., TJC) is deemed to meet Medicare CoPs without separate CMS survey.

questions.text: What is the primary purpose of a sentinel event review?

options.a: To determine financial liability for the event
options.b: To conduct a thorough root cause analysis and implement system improvements to prevent recurrence
options.c: To identify and discipline responsible staff members
options.d: To report the event to law enforcement

questions.explanation: Sentinel event reviews use root cause analysis to understand system-level factors contributing to serious events and develop corrective action plans.

questions.text: NCQA accreditation primarily applies to which type of healthcare organization?

options.b: Managed care organizations and health plans

questions.explanation: NCQA accredits managed care organizations, health plans, and disease management programs, focusing on quality of care and service.

questions.text: Which of the following BEST describes 'tracer methodology' used by The Joint Commission during surveys?

options.a: A process of reviewing financial documents to identify billing errors
options.b: Following the care experience of individual patients through the organization to assess compliance
options.c: Tracing the supply chain of medications used in the hospital
options.d: Reviewing staff training records for compliance

questions.explanation: Tracer methodology evaluates the care of individual patients by following their experiences across departments and staff, assessing compliance with standards in real care contexts.

questions.text: A hospital is preparing for a regulatory survey. Which approach BEST demonstrates a culture of continuous readiness?

options.a: Conducting intensive preparation activities only in the weeks before the survey
options.b: Maintaining ongoing compliance with standards through regular self-assessments and education
options.c: Hiring temporary staff to improve metrics before the survey
options.d: Limiting surveyor access to high-performing units

questions.explanation: Survey readiness as a continuous process — not just pre-survey cramming — reflects a true culture of quality and compliance.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of a 'structure' standard in accreditation?

options.a: Percentage of patients who received VTE prophylaxis
options.b: A requirement that hospitals have a functional quality improvement committee

questions.explanation: Structure standards address the organizational conditions for care, such as governance, committees, and staffing requirements — not the processes or outcomes of care.

questions.text: What does EMTALA require of hospital emergency departments?

options.a: To accept all patients regardless of their insurance status for any type of care
options.b: To provide medical screening and stabilizing treatment to all individuals regardless of ability to pay
options.c: To transfer all uninsured patients to publicly funded hospitals
options.d: To report all emergency visits to CMS within 24 hours

questions.explanation: EMTALA requires hospital EDs to provide a medical screening exam and necessary stabilizing treatment to any individual who presents, regardless of insurance status.

questions.text: Which accreditation body is responsible for accrediting home health agencies?
questions.explanation: The Joint Commission and the Accreditation Commission for Health Care (ACHC) both accredit home health agencies.

questions.text: A 'Plan of Correction' (POC) is required when:

options.a: A hospital voluntarily applies for a new accreditation program
options.b: Deficiencies or non-compliance are identified during a regulatory survey
options.c: A hospital implements a new quality improvement initiative

questions.explanation: A Plan of Correction formally documents how the organization will address identified deficiencies, with specific actions, timelines, and responsible parties.

questions.text: Which of the following is a key function of the hospital's quality committee related to regulatory compliance?

options.b: Overseeing compliance with accreditation standards and monitoring quality metrics

questions.explanation: The quality committee oversees compliance with regulatory and accreditation standards, reviews quality data, and guides improvement efforts.

questions.text: What is the role of a quality professional during a Joint Commission survey?

options.a: To speak on behalf of all staff and intercept all surveyor communications
options.b: To facilitate the survey process, provide requested documentation, and support staff
options.c: To prevent surveyors from accessing patient care areas
options.d: To negotiate the final survey score with the survey team

questions.explanation: Quality professionals facilitate the survey by coordinating logistics, ensuring documents are available, and supporting staff in responding to surveyor questions.

questions.text: Which of the following BEST describes the role of the Office of Inspector General (OIG) in healthcare?

options.a: Accrediting hospitals for quality and safety
options.b: Investigating and preventing fraud, waste, and abuse in federal healthcare programs
options.d: Approving new medical devices and pharmaceuticals

questions.explanation: The OIG focuses on combating fraud, waste, and abuse in Medicare, Medicaid, and other federal healthcare programs.
